title: Capstone: multiply on your own CPU
task: Set `PROGRAM` to an assembly program that multiplies the numbers at `X` and `Y` and leaves the product at `RESULT`, using only the 8 instructions (there's no multiply). It must set `RESULT` to 0 itself, handle `Y = 0`, and `HALT` when it's done.
hints: You need four data words after the HALT: `X: DATA 6`, `Y: DATA 7`, `RESULT: DATA 0`, plus the constants `ZERO: DATA 0` and `ONE: DATA 1`. Start with `LOAD ZERO` / `STORE RESULT`.

The loop starts at `LOOP: LOAD Y` / `JZ DONE`. The body has two parts: add X to RESULT (`LOAD RESULT`, `ADD X`, `STORE RESULT`), then count Y down (`LOAD Y`, `SUB ONE`, `STORE Y`). End it with `JMP LOOP`.
The whole program: `LOAD ZERO`, `STORE RESULT`, `LOOP: LOAD Y`, `JZ DONE`, `LOAD RESULT`, `ADD X`, `STORE RESULT`, `LOAD Y`, `SUB ONE`, `STORE Y`, `JMP LOOP`, `DONE: HALT`, then the data words.

quiz.q: Why do you need a `ONE: DATA 1` word to count down?

options.text: Every operand is an address, so SUB needs a memory word that holds 1
options.why: `SUB 1` would subtract whatever is stored at address 1, which is one of your instructions. Constants have to live in memory.

options.text: Because the CPU can't subtract small numbers
options.why: It can subtract any word. The issue is how it gets the number: from an address.

options.text: To keep the program 32 words long
options.why: The program can be any length up to 32. The constant is about how operands work.

quiz.q: Your loop checks `JZ DONE` at the top, before adding. What breaks if you check at the bottom instead?

options.text: With Y = 0, the body runs once, and Y wraps to 255, so you get 255 more adds
options.why: 0 − 1 wraps to 255 in 8 bits, so the loop keeps going for a long time and gives the wrong answer. Checking first handles zero.

options.text: Nothing: the result is the same
options.why: It's the same for every Y except 0. Try tracing it with Y = 0.
It assembles fine. It's a logic bug, which is worse: nothing warns you.
